chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

Regarding the woman whose menstrual blood stops in the last of her days, he said: 'If her husband experiences sexual desire (shabaq), let him order her to wash her private part, then he may touch her if he wishes before she performs the full ritual bath (ghusl).'

key_terms.تَغْتَسِلَ: she performs the full ritual bath (ghusl)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marital intimacy when a woman's menstrual period ends early or in the last days of her cycle?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the transitional state of purity (taharah) when menstruation ends before the customary period concludes, distinguishing between minor purification (washing the private part) and major purification (ghusl). It highlights the Shia juristic view that sexual intimacy is permissible once the bleeding ceases, even if the full ritual bath has not yet been performed, provided the woman has cleaned herself. This hadith is foundational in the chapter of childbirth and postpartum bleeding (nifas), illustrating the flexibility in marital relations during periods of uncertainty regarding menstrual boundaries.
